solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Received vehicle identifier, or wheels

indicators.note: wheels as a verb means turns round, so these letters spin into a new order

parts.note: REG is short for a car's registration, the plate that identifies it

explanation.surface: A radio operator acknowledges a message about a car's number plate, or perhaps its wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like a noun offered as an alternative, but it is the anagram signal working on REG plus OR.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio procedure the word is said to confirm a message has been heard and understood.

clue.text: Starts to rant on our message board

indicators.note: the starts of the next four words are taken, one initial from each

explanation.surface: Someone opens a furious thread on an online message board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like part of 'message board', but it is the definition, as in the phrase about lodging and meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging paired with meals is the idiom 'X and board', where both mean accommodation provided.

clue.text: I'm essential to running of errands

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone declares themselves indispensable to getting errands run.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks in the answer's own voice: 'I'm' is the definition, and the whole clue also describes such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The speaker is a dogsbody whose job is fetching and carrying, the person sent out on errands.

clue.text: Magazine runs article about idiots (about me)

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the bracketed about means the rearranged idiots are placed around the word me
the first about means the letters of idiots are turned around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A magazine publishes a piece about idiots, and the writer admits it is about themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does two jobs: the first one shuffles the idiots into DIOTIS, and the bracketed one wraps that round the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long-running British weekly listings magazine for television and radio schedules.

clue.text: Landowners almost appear uncomfortable with French art

indicators.note: almost says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to squirm is to wriggle and look ill at ease
es is French for 'art' in the old sense 'thou art', you are

explanation.surface: Rich landowners look awkward when faced with French paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is not painting but the archaic verb 'thou art'; in French 'tu es' gives ES. 'almost' drops the last M of SQUIRM.
explanation.definitionFit: Country gentlemen who held the chief estate of a parish were the traditional landed gentry.

clue.text: Hearty, as soldiers

parts.note: as can mean because, which is also since
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers described as hearty, robust fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty thanks or wishes are genuine and heartfelt ones, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Junkie's plan to completely drop resistance

definitions.note: Junkie's reads as 'Junkie is', the apostrophe s a link, so only the noun defines

indicators.note: dropping completely means sinking all the way to the bottom, so the letter goes to the end

parts.note: a ruse is a cunning plan or trick
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An addict's scheme to give up fighting the habit entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop resistance' suggests deleting R, but 'completely drop' sends the R of RUSE right down to the bottom of this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug addict is commonly called a drug taker, one who uses.

clue.text: Heading for Ypres front, put soldiers back in service

indicators.note: back says the whole string so far is read in the opposite direction, up this down light
the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the van is the front of an army or procession
to lay something is to put it down
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A First World War order: at the Ypres front, send troops back into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like military duty in general, but is the definition: one of the armed services. 'back' reverses Y+VAN+LAY+OR.
explanation.definitionFit: The navy is one of the three armed services, the senior one in Britain.

clue.text: Quiet hero rips open sheep

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: to rip open is to tear apart, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A violent scene: a hero tears a sheep apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheep' is not an animal being attacked but the definition, a breed named after an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hardy breed of sheep named after the English county where it was developed.

clue.text: Intimate with Italian poem about Italian poet

parts.note: con is the Italian word for with

indicators.note: about says the poem's title is turned round

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem
Dante is the poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A close friend of an Italian is reading a poem about Dante.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like an adjective or verb but is a noun: a close friend.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an intimate is a trusted close friend to whom secrets are told.

clue.text: Physician always backs court

indicators.note: backs says the letters run in reverse order

parts.note: DR is short for doctor
ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A doctor is a steady supporter of the court.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed open space beside a building is a courtyard, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Hollow ring found in wood

indicators.note: found in says the ring sits inside the wood

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A hollow ring of something is discovered in a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow' seems to describe the ring, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel or depression cut into a surface, a kind of hollow.

clue.text: One inclined to run on gas, ultimately

indicators.note: on says the running piece is placed after the gas piece
ultimately points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A person prone to running on gas, as if of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One inclined' suggests a person with a tendency, but it is literal: something that inclines.
explanation.definitionFit: An incline or slant is a surface that tilts, which is literally something inclined.

clue.text: Part of 7 game — press ahead

indicators.note: ahead says the pressing word goes in front of the game

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
bridge is the card game

explanation.surface: Part of a game where one must press ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 refers to the county answer at 7 down; this town is in it, named after the world's first cast-iron bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in the English county at 7 down grew up beside the famous iron span over the Severn gorge.

clue.text: Midlands newspaper piece about Reading MP among his constituents?

indicators.note: about says the piece wraps round everything that follows

parts.note: a bit is a piece
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs of schooling

indicators.note: constituents are the parts something is made from, here the letters reshuffled into a new form

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the MP for Reading mixing with voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the Berkshire town but gives R; 'constituents' looks like voters but is the anagram signal on MP AMONG HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a daily title published in England's second city, in the West Midlands.

clue.text: Splendid couple — more than one spoke

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent or splendid
II is the Roman numeral two

explanation.surface: A splendid couple, and more than one of them said something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like the past of speak but is the noun: a wheel spoke, which runs centre to rim.
explanation.definitionFit: A radius is a line from a circle's centre to its edge, like a wheel's spoke; this is its plural.

clue.text: Sci-fi hero in house after waving to crowd

indicators.note: after says the house piece comes after the waved letters
waving means moving to and fro, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sci-fi star stays indoors after waving to fans.
explanation.definitionFit: The time-travelling title character of the long-running BBC television series is a science fiction hero.

clue.text: Commemorations which could make you happiest

indicators.note: could make says the letters can be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Memorials that might cheer you up enormously.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that tombstone inscriptions are hardly cheering, yet their letters rearrange from happiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Inscriptions on tombs commemorate the dead, so they are a form of memorial.

clue.text: Old news about South American Indians televised

indicators.note: about says the two Ns go round the next pieces

parts.note: news is read as the plural of new, N, giving two Ns
S is the compass abbreviation for south
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: Old news about South American Indians has been broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is split as 'new' plus a plural, two Ns wrapped round S and CREE; the Cree are North, not South, American.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown on the screen means broadcast or seen on television, hence televised.

clue.text: She cooks everything, say, in turn

indicators.note: turn says the strung-together pieces are read backwards, up the light

parts.note: all means everything
EG, for example, is what say signals
taken as written

explanation.surface: She cooks everything, taking it all in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' looks like one phrase, but 'in' gives IN and 'turn' alone reverses ALL+EG+IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella Lawson is a celebrated British television cook, so the first name describes a woman who cooks.

clue.text: An official horse, some say

indicators.note: some say means some people pronounce it this way, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: Someone claims a horse has an official role.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the female horse and the civic head are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The elected head of a town council is a civic official.

clue.text: Bear, bee and bird

parts.note: the letter B is pronounced bee
a rook is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A list of three animals: a bear, a bee and a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate or put up with something is a formal verb sense, as in 'I will not stand for it'.

clue.text: River crew heads for eastern shore

parts.note: a gang is a crew of workers

indicators.note: heads for takes the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A boat crew on a river makes for the eastern bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The great sacred river of northern India, flowing into the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Oceanographer in Vietnam keeps keeling over

indicators.note: keeling over says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the name lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ocean scientist in Vietnam keeps capsizing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's hidden-word step had no indicator; 'in' is that indicator. Vagn Walfrid Ekman was a Swedish oceanographer (the Ekman spiral).
explanation.definitionFit: The Swede gave his name to the Ekman spiral and Ekman transport in ocean currents.

clue.text: See 13
Old Indian coin flipped to no effect?

indicators.note: flipping the word over changes nothing, so it reads the same either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Tossing an old Indian coin achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' suggests tossing a coin, but it means reversing the word, which leaves it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a former Indian currency unit, one sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Some had a wish to subdue once

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people had a wish to bring others under control in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an archaic word, found in Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: This obsolete verb meant to daunt or cow, which is to subdue.

clue.text: Some Americans make endless Han Solo cracks

indicators.note: cracks means breaks up, so the letters are reassembled
endless says the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Some Americans make jokes about the Star Wars character Han Solo, forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks' looks like jokes but is the anagram signal, on MAK (make, endless) plus HANSOLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of a particular US state are a subset of Americans.

clue.text: Conversely, English comic actor has new part

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so the letters are rearranged into a silly order
part of a word here is just its first letter

explanation.surface: An English comedy actor lands a new role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' looks like a description of the actor but is the anagram signal on ACTOR plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means on the contrary, the other way round, used in arguments.

clue.text: Manchester Evening News — it's for clever people

parts.note: MEN is the paper's initials
it is a slang word for sex appeal, SA

explanation.surface: A regional newspaper says it is aimed at intelligent readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is sex appeal, SA, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: The society admits only people with very high IQ scores, so it is a club for the intelligent.
